html:
The Rouran Khaganate was a nomadic confederation that ruled the Mongolian steppe from the late 300s to 555. The map shows it in 400 and 500. Chinese writers called them Ruanruan, "wriggling worms", as an insult.

Its rulers may have been the first to use the title khagan, later used by Turks and Mongols. The Rouran were the great northern rivals of the Northern Wei, the Xianbei dynasty that ruled north China. The Wei built walls and launched long campaigns against them, without ever destroying them. The Rouran in turn held the oasis states of the Tarim Basin and allied with the Hephthalites further west.

Among their subjects were the Türks, who worked iron for them in the Altai. In 552 the Türk leader Bumin rose and defeated the Rouran, and by 555 their state was gone, replaced by the Türk Khaganates. Some historians think the Avars who reached Europe soon after were Rouran refugees, but this is not proven.
